milestones.title: M00 Repository Recovery and Reference Trust
milestones.description: Restore a truthful, reproducible CLROS baseline and a durable issue inventory. Milestones carry no fabricated due date and close only from preserved evidence.
milestones.exitCriteria: Restore a truthful, reproducible CLROS baseline and a durable issue inventory.

milestones.title: M01 Live Boot Memory and Paging
milestones.description: Prove owned reservations, allocation, paging, CR3, and W^X under real QEMU. Milestones carry no fabricated due date and close only from preserved evidence.
milestones.exitCriteria: Prove owned reservations, allocation, paging, CR3, and W^X under real QEMU.

milestones.title: M02 Owned x64 Diagnostics
milestones.description: Prove owned COM1 and descriptor/fault handling under real QEMU. Milestones carry no fabricated due date and close only from preserved evidence.
milestones.exitCriteria: Prove owned COM1 and descriptor/fault handling under real QEMU.

milestones.title: M03 Real Firmware Exit
milestones.description: Exit UEFI boot services and retain owned memory, diagnostics, and platform snapshots. Milestones carry no fabricated due date and close only from preserved evidence.
milestones.exitCriteria: Exit UEFI boot services and retain owned memory, diagnostics, and platform snapshots.

milestones.title: M04 NativeAOT Runtime Correctness
milestones.description: Replace fail-fast runtime helpers only after host and guest evidence. Milestones carry no fabricated due date and close only from preserved evidence.
milestones.exitCriteria: Replace fail-fast runtime helpers only after host and guest evidence.

milestones.title: M05 Platform, PCI, and Common Virtio
milestones.description: Cross the live ACPI, PCI, DMA, and common virtio device boundary. Milestones carry no fabricated due date and close only from preserved evidence.
milestones.exitCriteria: Cross the live ACPI, PCI, DMA, and common virtio device boundary.

milestones.title: M06 Live Storage
milestones.description: Read the packaged manifest and payload from live virtio-blk after firmware exit. Milestones carry no fabricated due date and close only from preserved evidence.
milestones.exitCriteria: Read the packaged manifest and payload from live virtio-blk after firmware exit.

milestones.title: M07 Live Networking
milestones.description: Exchange live virtio-net traffic through bounded TCP and HTTP. Milestones carry no fabricated due date and close only from preserved evidence.
milestones.exitCriteria: Exchange live virtio-net traffic through bounded TCP and HTTP.

milestones.title: M08 Native Workload Execution
milestones.description: Load and execute one disk-backed freestanding C# NativeAOT workload. Milestones carry no fabricated due date and close only from preserved evidence.
milestones.exitCriteria: Load and execute one disk-backed freestanding C# NativeAOT workload.

milestones.title: M09 Scheduler, PAL, and Hosted CoreCLR
milestones.description: Implement scheduler/threading primitives for the M16 NativeAOT-first route now. The historical milestone title and later CoreCLR children remain for framework-dependent hosting; CoreCLR completion is not a prerequisite for M10 Kestrel. See docs/workload-profiles.md. Close only from preserved evidence for all retained children.
milestones.exitCriteria: Prove scheduler/PAL primitives and a separately built .NET 11 CoreCLR Hello workload.

milestones.title: M10 Local SingleMinimalApi Kestrel
milestones.description: Serve the deterministic health response from real upstream .NET 11 NativeAOT Kestrel through the M16 Linux socket/epoll adapters and continuing CLROS TCP. Qualify local SingleMinimalApi with external HTTP evidence before multi-process or provider work; no CoreCLR prerequisite.
milestones.exitCriteria: Serve the deterministic Minimal API health response through live CLROS sockets.

milestones.title: M11 Images, CI, and Security
milestones.description: Make local artifacts, CI evidence, and release security reproducible and honest. Milestones carry no fabricated due date and close only from preserved evidence.
milestones.exitCriteria: Make local artifacts, CI evidence, and release security reproducible and honest.

milestones.title: M12 AWS Nitro Validation
milestones.description: Boot and serve SingleMinimalApi on AWS Nitro through ENA and NVMe. Milestones carry no fabricated due date and close only from preserved evidence.
milestones.exitCriteria: Boot and serve SingleMinimalApi on AWS Nitro through ENA and NVMe.

milestones.title: M13 Azure VM Validation
milestones.description: Boot and serve SingleMinimalApi on Azure through VMBus, NetVSC, and StorVSC. Milestones carry no fabricated due date and close only from preserved evidence.
milestones.exitCriteria: Boot and serve SingleMinimalApi on Azure through VMBus, NetVSC, and StorVSC.

milestones.title: M14 MultiMinimalApi Isolation
milestones.description: Mandatory second target after M10: prove two separately packaged NativeAOT Minimal API processes and crash containment locally through M14-016 before AWS/Azure qualification. Provider repeats M14-017/018 follow their own provider gates; milestone-wide closure still requires those later repeats.
milestones.exitCriteria: Prove two isolated Minimal API workloads and crash containment locally and on both providers.

milestones.title: M15 Production and Hosted-Tier Expansion
milestones.description: Add production recovery, provenance, sustained tests, and optional hosted workloads. Milestones carry no fabricated due date and close only from preserved evidence.
milestones.exitCriteria: Add production recovery, provenance, sustained tests, and optional hosted workloads.

milestones.title: M16 NativeAOT Linux ABI Foundation
milestones.description: Priority foundation for one upstream .NET 11 NativeAOT Minimal API on the C# CLROS kernel. Numeric milestone order is not execution order. CoreCLR and broad Linux compatibility are deferred.
milestones.exitCriteria: Pinned ELF payload, continuing post-exit execution, user boundary, upstream runtime qualification, Linux sockets and epoll are evidenced under QEMU; M10 separately accepts Kestrel.

implementationNotes: Implement a standalone C# 14/.NET 10 host tool with no first-party C, C++, header, assembly, or checked-in object file. Generated .obj output is ephemeral under obj or an explicit caller-selected temporary output path.

Emit AMD64 COFF machine 0x8664 with timestamp zero and exactly three file-backed sections. .text$clrossm has raw size 20 and exactly the required IMAGE_SCN_CNT_CODE, IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ, IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE, and IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_16BYTES characteristics with IMAGE_SCN_MEM_WRITE clear; it also lacks initialized/uninitialized-data, COMDAT, remove, discardable, and relocation-overflow flags. .xdata$clrossm has raw size 8 and .pdata$clrossm has raw size 12; each has IMAGE_SCN_CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA, IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ, and IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_4BYTES with IMAGE_SCN_MEM_WRITE and IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE clear and lacks code, COMDAT, remove, discardable, and relocation-overflow flags. Every required raw-data and relocation range is nonzero, in bounds, mutually nonoverlapping, and overflow checked. Emit no imports, directives, COMDAT ambiguity, debug records, writable/executable section, or unrelated external symbol.

Export exactly one external symbol named CLROS_X64_SerializeInstructionPublication with external storage class, .text$clrossm section number, value zero, COFF function type 0x20, no auxiliary record, and no weak-external or alias fallback. Define the relocation-only .xdata$clrossm base symbol with static storage class, its exact section number, value zero, and no auxiliary/weak/alias fallback; it is not an additional external symbol. The exact 20 function bytes are 53 B8 00 00 00 00 B9 00 00 00 00 0F A2 B8 43 4C 52 53 5B C3: push RBX, load CPUID leaf/subleaf zero with flag-neutral MOV immediates, execute exactly one CPUID, load success cookie 0x53524C43 in EAX, restore RBX, and return.

Emit exact UNWIND_INFO bytes 01 01 01 00 01 30 00 00: version 1, flags zero, one-byte prolog, one unwind code, no frame register, UWOP_PUSH_NONVOL RBX at code offset 1, and zero padding. Emit one 12-byte RUNTIME_FUNCTION raw record with begin addend 0, end addend 20, and unwind addend 0. Its only relocations are IMAGE_REL_AMD64_ADDR32NB at .pdata offsets 0 and 4 against the external function symbol and at offset 8 against one static value-zero .xdata$clrossm base symbol; text and xdata have no relocations and no additional external symbol is permitted.

The generated Windows-x64 function has a valid push-RBX prolog and pop-RBX/ret epilog and restores RSP and RBX exactly. The object encodes the complete RUNTIME_FUNCTION/UNWIND_INFO intent required for asynchronous unwind coverage at every instruction boundary, but M01-033 must not claim final unwindability before linker relocation and M01-034 final-artifact verification. PUSH/POP, MOV, and CPUID preserve RFLAGS; RAX returns the fixed cookie; only volatile RCX and RDX remain clobbered. It performs no calls, conditional branches, runtime-helper access, or privileged-pointer access.

Build an independent bounds-checked host parser in the focused test rather than trusting the writer's object model. Parse the COFF header, all three section tables and raw-data ranges, relocation tables, symbol table, auxiliary count, long section/symbol names, and string table before comparing the complete text, unwind, runtime-function, relocation, symbol, and flag contracts. The focused test must clean-build and invoke the standalone generator through a bounded subprocess so a clean HostTests build/run does not depend on stale tool output; do not add a HostTests project reference or make the generator a transitive CLROS.slnx dependency in this leaf.

implementationNotes: Use only the immutable M01-034 direct static extern uint InternalCall binding and compare every returned value to its exact 0x53524C43 success constant. Never copy the serializer bytes into LoaderCode, generate a second barrier, use a firmware callback as a barrier, ignore or synthesize the return value, or execute the serializer from a page that the current epoch just modified.

Maintain the four-bit publication mask in explicit EfiEntry-owned static or boot-handoff-owned primitive state that survives the one-way stage-one stack switch; an ordinary caller local is forbidden. Clear and validate the state once before epoch 1, reject stale/nonzero or repeated initialization, and require exact successful transitions 0 -> 1 -> 3 -> 7 -> 15. Epoch 1 is the stage-one stack-probe publication: call exactly once after the last probe byte write, full readback, and binding installation; reject a wrong cookie without entering the probe; then transition 0 -> 1 before any indirect transfer can enter it.

Epoch 2 is the stage-one stack-switch publication: call exactly once after the prepared stack-switch bytes are fully copied and read back; reject a wrong cookie without obtaining/invoking switchEntry; then transition 1 -> 3 before the one-way transfer to the owned-stack continuation. The continuation must observe the same EfiEntry-owned/handoff-owned state rather than reconstructing or trusting a local mask.

Epoch 3 is the stage-three initial publication group inside CaptureArchitecturalPreflight. Refactor that boundary so preparation writes and fully validates the transfer thunk, planner thunk, paging-preflight, and PAT-reader streams and binds both preflight and PAT entry addresses without invoking either entry. After the PAT-reader readback loop and both entry bindings, while the mask is exactly 3, call the serializer once, reject a wrong cookie without executing either entry, transition 3 -> 7, and only then invoke preflight followed by PAT. No generated entry, firmware callback, unrelated managed call, executable-byte write, binding mutation, or readback mutation may occur between the successful cookie check and first preflight invocation. A caller-side barrier after CaptureArchitecturalPreflight returns is too late and must fail source tests.

Epoch 4 is the stage-three final publication group: call exactly once after the final composite, call-gate, and constant-return protection-probe write/readback and binding step, after existing M01_PRE_CR3 firmware output; reject a wrong cookie without invoking the call gate; then transition 7 -> 15 and immediately enter the call gate. No executable-page write, rebinding, firmware callback, or unrelated managed call may occur between the successful check and first execution.

Every cookie mismatch emits stable M01_INSTRUCTION_PUBLICATION_COOKIE_FAILED before cleanup and prevents that epoch's generated code from executing. Only after epoch 4 returns, firmware CR3/CR4/RFLAGS are restored, the continuation canary passes, and the mask is exactly 0xF may EfiEntry emit M01_INSTRUCTION_PUBLICATION_EPOCHS_VERIFIED immediately before M01_POST_CR3.

Preserve all default-off behavior, stage prerequisites, failure cleanup, firmware-callback exclusions, and preexisting marker order apart from the two explicit new marker contracts. The serializer itself emits no marker and performs no allocation, exception, reflection, managed callback, firmware call, or diagnostic I/O.

Source-order tests identify each epoch structurally and prove final write/readback/binding precedes exactly one serializer call, its returned cookie is consumed and compared, the exact mask transition occurs only after success, and every possible first execution follows that check. They must prove the state is explicitly cleared and validated before epoch 1, survives the one-way switch, follows only 0 -> 1 -> 3 -> 7 -> 15, and cannot be reconstructed or pre-set in the owned-stack continuation. They must locate epoch 3 inside CaptureArchitecturalPreflight after PAT readback and both entry bindings but before the current preflight(observation) and readPat() calls. They must not accept comments, string literals, a method with a similar name, an ignored/synthetic cookie, a pre-set bit, a caller-side epoch-3 barrier after method return, or a barrier placed only on one branch.

Mutation tests remove, duplicate, reorder, or move each call early; move epoch 3 outside or after CaptureArchitecturalPreflight; ignore, replace, or compare the return against zero/default/wrong cookie; use an ordinary local mask across the one-way switch; omit or repeat reset; seed stale state; skip, repeat, regress, or reorder any 0 -> 1 -> 3 -> 7 -> 15 transition; set a mask bit without a successful call; emit the aggregate marker early or with a partial mask; insert a byte write/readback/binding after the call; execute before the check; substitute CPUID bytes in the dynamic page, LFENCE, MFENCE, volatile access, lock-prefixed data access, an ordinary managed call, or a firmware callback; bypass the call on success/error/default paths; or bind a zero/default/wrong function. Every mutation must fail with the affected epoch identified.

Positive and negative tests also cover zero-length/default plans, partial publication, malformed/truncated byte sources, overflowed destination ranges, readback mismatch, cleanup/timeout paths, disabled probes, repeated invocation, and all four publication epochs enabled together.

Build a fresh all-three-switch EFI artifact and require M01-034 artifact verification. The mandatory EFI preflight may query only qemu-system-x86_64 --version and qemu-img --version for tool discovery; no QEMU smoke, guest boot, or QEMU dry-run smoke workflow may run, and neither version probes nor build/source ordering may be interpreted as empirical SCSB, cross-core, or live-CR3 evidence.

acceptanceCriteria: Focused source tests prove exactly four immutable-serializer call sites, one at each named publication epoch, after the complete final write/readback/binding; each call's uint result must equal 0x53524C43 and advance one shared EfiEntry-owned/handoff-owned state through exactly 0 -> 1 -> 3 -> 7 -> 15 before every possible first execution. The state is cleared and validated before epoch 1 and demonstrably survives the one-way stack switch.

Epoch 3 is proven inside CaptureArchitecturalPreflight after its PAT-reader readback loop and both entry-address bindings but before the current preflight(observation) and readPat() calls; a barrier in the caller after CaptureArchitecturalPreflight returns is rejected as too late.

Epoch 4 ordering specifically preserves existing M01_PRE_CR3 output before serialization, rejects a wrong cookie without entering owned CR3, and permits no executable write, readback mutation, rebinding, firmware callback, or unrelated managed call between the successful check and audited call-gate invocation.

Mutation tests reject missing, duplicate, early, late, branch-only, ignored/synthetic/wrong-cookie, pre-set/partial-mask, early aggregate marker, dynamically generated, wrong-binding, no-op, CPUID-in-published-stream-only, LFENCE/MFENCE/volatile/lock/ordinary-call/firmware-callback substitutes and identify the affected epoch.
Positive, malformed-input, zero/default, overflow, partial-write, readback-mismatch, timeout/cleanup, disabled-path, repeated-call, and all-switch tests preserve prior marker order and fail closed.

A fresh canonical all-three-switch EFI build and M01-034 final-artifact/unwind verifier pass. Source tests prove M01_INSTRUCTION_PUBLICATION_COOKIE_FAILED dominates cleanup on mismatch and M01_INSTRUCTION_PUBLICATION_EPOCHS_VERIFIED is emitted only for mask 0xF after post-return restoration/canary validation and immediately before M01_POST_CR3. The mandatory EFI preflight may query only qemu-system-x86_64 --version and qemu-img --version for tool discovery; no QEMU smoke, guest boot, or QEMU dry-run smoke workflow may run, and no version probe or guest marker is treated as runtime evidence by this issue.

Only EfiEntry, the focused source/mutation test, and canonical boot/architecture/security docs change; OS.csproj, CLROS.slnx, generator, targets, RuntimeImport declaration, verifier, QEMU runner, and completion gates remain untouched.

The evidence explicitly does not prove empirical absence of speculative stale-instruction execution, cross-core publication, coherent DMA-written code, hardware execution, live CR3, permanent W^X, or any M01 completion gate.

Reuse X64ThreadContext (688 bytes), OSHostHandle generation/slot shape, ReadyQueue and DeadlineQueue. Slot generations and wait sequence identities must fail closed at exhaustion rather than wrap into a stale identity. A wait identity distinguishes successive waits by one still-live thread. Do not reuse OSHostThreadTable's managed mock implementation or advertise hosted-runtime readiness.

Keep IRQ-off CPL0 Entry/CapturedCall admission. Define a measured Win64 first-entry trampoline and normal-return-to-exit path, stack alignment, shadow space, executable mapping and x87/SSE/FS/GS ownership. Preserve the separate 704-byte timer frame and IRETQ rules; never reinterpret arbitrary interrupted state as a CALL continuation. No asynchronous resumption of arbitrary C# workers, AVX/XSAVE, CET or SMP in this slice.

One supervisor owns every state/queue/lifetime change. Save/disable/restore IF around the entire check-register-park or wake/cancel/exit transaction. Publish only fully initialized runnable contexts. Reserve ready capacity before consuming a due deadline or retain a pending completion for retry; no lost wake on a full queue. Define explicitly how stale queue heads are removed by their owner.

Sleep accepts ticks in one checked nonwrapping epoch, not wall-clock milliseconds. Delay zero yields without registering a deadline. Implement repeated timer ownership: a documented Restore/Prepare(saved tick)/Arm sequence or a narrowly tested rearm operation. WakeReady alone is not a reusable timer. Provide a retained owned idle/dispatcher path with interrupts enabled while all workers are parked; no busy-wait substitute for a hardware wake.

Define join as at most one pending waiter per target for this slice. Self-join and cyclic join chains reject before parking; another pending waiter returns an explicit status. Exit status is retained and repeated completed joins may observe it until explicit supervisor reap. Join timeout/cancellation releases only the wait registration and does not implicitly cancel the target. Each wait has exactly one completion winner among wake, exit, cancellation and deadline.

Cancellation is a deferred request observed at start or a documented cooperative safe point. A parked worker resumes with a cancellation result and reaches its exit path; never free a running or interrupted stack. Exit transfers to a retained owner context before teardown. Reap is supervisor-only after ready/deadline/join and IRQ/context/root-lifetime references are gone; only then scrub/release storage and advance the slot generation. Model lifetime pins without adding upstream GC or stop-the-world scanning.

supplementalIssues.title: [M06 reference adaptation] Add bounded in-place FAT32 boot-log writes on a real filesystem image
supplementalIssues.body:
<!-- clros-supplemental-scope:sharpos-fat32-inplace-bootlog -->
## Purpose

Add the smallest failure-contained write path that can preserve a bounded post-firmware boot log: overwrite bytes inside one existing preallocated FAT32 file, never grow it or allocate clusters, and prove the resulting raw image bytes after a fresh real-QEMU/OVMF boot. This closes a real gap in the current read-only M06 ladder without turning CLROS into a general writable filesystem.

This is a supplemental issue outside `.gitea/backlog/clros-issues.json`. It remains `agent:blocked`; do not claim it before its dependencies and collision lanes are clear.

## SharpOS provenance and attribution

SharpOS step 149 introduced a deliberately narrow write primitive and a bounded boot-log sink after a physical-hardware investigation.

- Upstream commit: `https://github.com/daniilvaino/SharpOS/commit/934b4fd8e4e8849d13d774bacfef063870a18d05`.
- FAT32 source: `https://github.com/daniilvaino/SharpOS/blob/934b4fd8e4e8849d13d774bacfef063870a18d05/OS/src/Hal/Fat32.cs#L659-L746`; SHA-256 `FE60240E80E303D2B5038F3711458FCF087CE6AC9907A981C82B92DC7401F310`.
- Boot-log source: `https://github.com/daniilvaino/SharpOS/blob/934b4fd8e4e8849d13d774bacfef063870a18d05/OS/src/Hal/BootLog.cs#L16-L93`; SHA-256 `5D63816D89B6E8873A98D3CD0EB385993F80FA6B606821267C37FF9FF1DE2C82`.
- SharpOS-authored source is covered by the recorded owner grant and upstream CC0-1.0 evidence in `docs/license-audit.md`. Retain this commit/path/hash attribution. Do not copy unrelated vendor or application code.

Minimum excerpts identifying the safety boundary:

```csharp
if ((uint)len > size) return -1;
if (!wholeSector) ReadSector();
```

```csharp
if (s_sector >= s_sectorCount) return;
WriteSectorAt(s_startLba + s_sector);
```

## Dependencies

- #122/M06-007: live device behind the accepted read-only block contract.
- #126/M06-011: locate the FAT32 application/EFI partition.
- #127/M06-012: checked cluster-chain walking with loop/bad-cluster/truncation handling.
- #133/M06-018: diagnosable post-EBS malformed-storage failures.
- Accepted M03 post-EBS owned diagnostics and M05 PCI/DMA/virtio common-device prerequisites.
- A collision-safe integration lane must be available for `BootSequence.cs`, EFI/QEMU scripts, image-builder staging, and canonical shared docs. Those paths are forbidden to the host leaf until a supplemental integration scope is claimed.

## Exact host-leaf owned paths

- `src/OS.Kernel/Storage/IWritableBlockDevice.cs`
- `src/OS.Kernel/Storage/VirtioBlockWriteRequestPlan.cs`
- `src/OS.Kernel/Storage/Fat32InPlaceWriter.cs`
- `src/OS.Kernel/Diagnostics/BoundedBootLogSink.cs`
- `tests/OS.HostTests/Fat32InPlaceWriterTests.cs`
- `tests/OS.HostTests/BoundedBootLogSinkTests.cs`
- `docs/cstorage.md`
- `docs/image-builder.md`
- exactly one newly reserved `done/stepNN.md`, only after implementation/evidence exist

## Read-only inputs

- Existing `IReadOnlyBlockDevice`, `Fat32Parser`, FAT32 status/result types, GPT/ESP selection contracts, virtio-blk request plans, diagnostic byte writers, and image-builder contracts.
- `docs/license-audit.md`, `docs/completion-gates.md`, and the two upstream files above.

## Forbidden to the host leaf

- `src/OS/Boot/EfiEntry.cs`, `src/OS/OS.csproj`
- `src/OS.Kernel/Boot/BootSequence.cs`
- `src/OS.Kernel/Diagnostics/Probes.cs`
- current live virtio implementations, shared build/QEMU/image scripts, workflows, PAL ABI files, apps, references, artifacts, README, completion-gate edits, and every existing done step
- any `OS.*`, `src/OS`, `src/OS.Kernel`, or `OSHost_*` rename

## CLROS adaptation contract

Do not copy the SharpOS static filesystem/global-buffer implementation. Build caller-owned, status-coded CLROS contracts:

```csharp
public interface IWritableBlockDevice : IReadOnlyBlockDevice
{
    BlockWriteResult WriteBlocks(ulong lba, ReadOnlySpan<byte> source);
}

public readonly struct Fat32InPlaceWriteRequest
{
    public ulong PartitionStartLba { get; }
    public ReadOnlyMemory<byte> Path { get; }
    public ReadOnlyMemory<byte> Source { get; }
    public bool RequireContiguousClusters { get; }
}

public static Fat32InPlaceWriteResult WriteExistingFile(
    IWritableBlockDevice device,
    in Fat32InPlaceWriteRequest request,
    Span<byte> sectorScratch);
```

Required behavior:

1. Resolve only an existing regular file using current checked FAT32 parsing. Reject missing files, directories, unsupported names/paths, zero/default BPB geometry, invalid start cluster, loops, bad/reserved clusters, and chain truncation.
2. The initial contract requires a contiguous checked chain. Never assume contiguity; prove each next cluster is exactly current+1 or return `FragmentedFileUnsupported` before writing.
3. Never grow the file, alter directory entries, allocate/free clusters, modify FAT entries, change file length/timestamps, or write outside the file's existing data clusters.
4. Require `source.Length <= existingFileSize` and checked sector/LBA arithmetic. Zero-length writes succeed without device I/O.
5. Full sectors write directly from caller-owned bounded buffers. A partial first/tail sector must read-modify-write and preserve every byte outside the requested range.
6. Return exact bytes completed (durability requires a separately proven flush contract) and the failing LBA/status on short write, timeout, reset, read-before-partial failure, or device removal. No exception, retry loop, hidden allocation, or success after partial failure.
7. `BoundedBootLogSink` binds once to a manifest-selected, preallocated file. It uses a caller-owned fixed buffer, strips or explicitly encodes CR/LF, never wraps when capacity is reached, guards reentrancy, and disables further disk writes after the first device failure while owned serial diagnostics continue.
8. Do not log secrets, environment data, credentials, provider metadata, raw application payloads, or unbounded panic memory. Release policy must be documented.
9. The host leaf models virtio write request direction/status/timeout but performs no live device I/O.

## Host tests

Include exact single-sector/full-sector, unaligned partial head/tail, multi-sector, zero-length, file-size boundary, missing/directory/path rejection, fragmented/loop/bad/truncated chain, LBA overflow, scratch-too-small, read-before-partial failure, short/failed write, no out-of-range writes, unchanged FAT/directory sectors, log capacity/no-wrap, reentrancy, disable-after-failure, and warmed allocation tests.

```text
TEST_START m06.fat32-bootlog
CLROS_M06_FAT32_BOOTLOG_READY inPlaceOnly=true contiguousVerified=true fileGrowth=false hostOnly=true
TEST_PASS m06.fat32-bootlog
```

## Serialized real-QEMU integration requirement

Before this issue can close, create/claim a collision-safe supplemental integration issue that:

1. Stages a fixed-size, contiguous `CLROS/BOOTLOG.TXT` fixture in the repository's real GPT/FAT32 raw image; VVFAT/directory passthrough is forbidden evidence.
2. Adds the minimal live virtio-blk write operation and wires the sink in `BootSequence.cs` only after post-EBS owned diagnostics and FAT32 mount are valid.

4. Reboots the mutated image read-only and verifies the exact record/hash.

```text
FAT32_BOOTLOG_WRITE_FAILED
```

6. Captures exact source head, EFI/raw-image before/after, serial log, QEMU stdout/stderr/summary, changed-LBA ledger, target-file before/after, and reboot-verification SHA-256 hashes.

Provider or physical USB/NVMe writes are not required to accept the QEMU slice and must never be inferred from it.

Independent exact-head review is required before merge/closure.

This issue does not prove a general writable filesystem, crash-consistent metadata updates, journaling, arbitrary fragmented writes, USB/NVMe/AHCI support, provider storage, real ExitBootServices by itself, hosted .NET, Kestrel, CloudReady status, or production readiness.

<!-- clros-canonical-review:2026-10-23 -->

Report bytes completed separately from durable bytes; require negotiated device flush/barrier and restart evidence for durability. This preallocated overwrite scope cannot substitute for create/grow/delete/locking/SQLite storage.

supplementalIssues.body:
<!-- clros-supplemental-scope:sharpos-usb-host-discovery -->
## Purpose

Preserve the useful part of SharpOS step 149 USB bring-up: bounded PCI discovery of USB host controllers, explicit scan-truncation evidence, and xHCI classification. This is an optional physical-bring-up aid. It is not a USB driver, boot-media path, or CLROS completion-gate prerequisite.

Dependencies #94 and #97-#101 are accepted. This supplemental issue is `agent:ready`; claim its host leaf only when its declared paths are collision-free, and claim a separate integration issue before guest wiring.

## Upstream provenance and license

- Commit: `https://github.com/daniilvaino/SharpOS/commit/934b4fd8e4e8849d13d774bacfef063870a18d05`.
- USB discovery: `https://github.com/daniilvaino/SharpOS/blob/934b4fd8e4e8849d13d774bacfef063870a18d05/OS/src/Hal/Usb/UsbHost.cs#L35-L72`; SHA-256 `446F7C7C9BF372564AB1D16116F792539D6F466C7EAA68DC31C3A696EF597715`.

- SharpOS-authored source is covered by the recorded owner grant/upstream CC0-1.0 evidence. Keep commit/path/hash attribution; do not import other vendor/device code.

Minimum upstream excerpt:

```csharp
if (d.ClassID != 0x0C || d.SubClassID != 0x03) continue;
c.Kind = (Kind)d.ProgIF;
```

## Dependencies

- #97/M05-004 bounded PCI configuration-space interface.
- #98/M05-005 live ECAM header read.
- #99/M05-006 bounded bus/device/function enumeration with diagnostics.
- #100/M05-007 malformed/cyclic PCI capability tests.
- #101/M05-008 BAR sizing/restoration before any MMIO claim.
- #94/M05-001 explicit UC/WC/WB mapping policy before future xHCI MMIO access.

No USB issue may bypass or silently widen the accepted PCI enumeration bounds.

## Exact host-leaf owned paths

- `src/OS.Kernel/Platform/Usb/UsbHostControllerDiscoveryPlan.cs`
- `src/OS.Kernel/Platform/Usb/UsbHostControllerKind.cs`
- `tests/OS.HostTests/UsbHostControllerDiscoveryPlanTests.cs`
- `docs/drivers.md`
- exactly one new `done/stepNN.md`, reserved only after implementation/evidence exist

## Read-only and forbidden paths

Read-only: existing PCI descriptor/BAR/address contracts, M05 mapping/DMA contracts, `docs/license-audit.md`, `docs/completion-gates.md`, and the upstream files.

Forbidden to this host leaf: active ECAM/MMIO code, `BootSequence.cs`, `Probes.cs`, `EfiEntry.cs`, `OS.csproj`, QEMU/image scripts, PAL ABI, storage, apps, references, generated artifacts, README, completion-gate changes, and existing done steps. Preserve `OS.*`, `src/OS`, `src/OS.Kernel`, and every `OSHost_*` identity.

## CLROS adaptation contract

```csharp
public enum UsbHostControllerKind : byte
{
    Uhci = 0x00,
    Ohci = 0x10,
    Ehci = 0x20,
    Xhci = 0x30,
    Unknown = 0xFF
}

public static UsbDiscoveryResult Discover(
    ReadOnlySpan<PciFunctionDescriptor> functions,
    Span<UsbHostControllerDescriptor> destination,
    in PciEnumerationCoverage coverage);
```

Required behavior:

1. Accept only PCI class `0x0C` and subclass `0x03`; classify programming-interface values `0x00/0x10/0x20/0x30` explicitly and preserve unknown values without treating them as usable.
2. Return BDF, vendor/device IDs, programming interface, BAR metadata, controller count, required capacity, enumeration coverage, and a distinct `Truncated` status.
3. Never say “no controllers” when PCI enumeration or the destination buffer truncated. `CompleteNoControllers`, `ControllersFound`, `InputEnumerationTruncated`, and `DestinationTooSmall` are separate outcomes.
4. Validate duplicate BDFs, multifunction functions, 32/64-bit BAR pairing, I/O BAR rejection, zero/unassigned BARs, address overflow, and MMIO alignment. Do not size a BAR here and do not write PCI configuration space.
5. Bound all loops by caller-provided spans and accepted PCI coverage. No hidden allocation, exception, reflection, dynamic invocation, or static mutable device registry.
6. The host leaf performs no MMIO, reset, BIOS handoff, ring allocation, doorbell access, port enumeration, transfer, interrupt setup, or boot-media I/O.

## Host evidence

Tests must cover UHCI/OHCI/EHCI/xHCI/unknown classification, mixed non-USB functions, zero controllers with complete coverage, zero controllers with truncated coverage, capacity exhaustion, duplicate BDF, malformed BARs, 64-bit BAR overflow, deterministic ordering, failure atomicity, and allocation-free warmed execution.

```text
TEST_START m05.usb-discovery
CLROS_M05_USB_DISCOVERY_READY kinds=5 truncationExplicit=true mmioTouched=false hostOnly=true
TEST_PASS m05.usb-discovery
```

## Real-QEMU integration requirement

Before closing, a separately claimed integration issue must add a deterministic QEMU profile containing an xHCI controller, rebuild from the exact source head, run real QEMU/OVMF, consume the accepted live PCI census, and emit exactly one ordered marker:

```text
CLROS_M05_USB_DISCOVERY_READY xhci=1 coverageComplete=true scanTruncated=false mmioTouched=false guestIntegrated=true
USB_DISCOVERY_FAILED
```

The profile must also prove the zero-controller complete case and a synthetic/truncated negative case, with all `TEST_FAIL` and the issue failure marker forbidden. Capture source/artifact/image/serial/QEMU hashes and exact QEMU device arguments. `-DryRun` is preflight only.

Physical-machine evidence is optional and distinct: record machine/firmware identity, complete PCI coverage, and controller descriptors. Do not infer USB storage, keyboard, xHCI initialization, Azure/AWS support, or production readiness from discovery.

## Documentation, acceptance, and boundary

Update `docs/drivers.md` with implemented classification, bounds, unsupported operations, QEMU command, and hardware/provider boundary. Reserve one unique done step. Run focused tests, full solution/HostTests, naming/source firewall, fresh QEMU profile, `git diff --check`, ownership audit, and independent exact-head review.

Acceptance is bounded host classification plus fresh QEMU live-PCI discovery. This issue does not implement a USB stack, xHCI registers/rings, interrupts, transfers, mass storage, USB boot logging, physical/provider support, hosted .NET, Kestrel, CloudReady status, production readiness, or a completion-gate advance.

supplementalIssues.body:
<!-- clros-supplemental-scope:sharpos-terminal-console-input -->
## Purpose

Define the bounded console-input, wait, and serialized terminal-feed semantics needed by an optional hosted interactive workload such as PowerShell/PSReadLine. This preserves the useful concepts from SharpOS steps 144-147 without importing a desktop terminal stack, exposing a login shell, or making terminal support part of CLROS's default single-workload cloud profile.

This is a supplemental optional issue. Keep it `agent:blocked`; it is not an M09/Kestrel/production gate prerequisite.

## Provenance and license boundaries

SharpOS-authored glue/behavior inputs:

- Step 147 commit: `https://github.com/daniilvaino/SharpOS/commit/b98237b04bd06efb4090ca5ddd492b392b098093`.
- Serialized terminal feed: `https://github.com/daniilvaino/SharpOS/blob/934b4fd8e4e8849d13d774bacfef063870a18d05/OS/src/Hal/TerminalConsole.cs#L102-L139`; SHA-256 `4B81E4B76293DEE3DBCE3F9E0AD1120E6B082F8F4833F24274E40772C5D36690`.
- Console input translation: `https://github.com/daniilvaino/SharpOS/blob/934b4fd8e4e8849d13d774bacfef063870a18d05/OS/src/PAL/SharpOSHost/ConsoleInput.cs`; SHA-256 `B3A57F953DA58572D94DBEBEAAD91ED1F044D1B4AFA780442FF9CECF5C9F7810`.
- Wait semantics: `https://github.com/daniilvaino/SharpOS/blob/934b4fd8e4e8849d13d774bacfef063870a18d05/OS/src/PAL/SharpOSHost/ThreadStubs.cs#L223-L305`; SHA-256 `A2D75EDA1AD44ECDE89151B88175C99739778CE9BE6A93EA052CDF99B7A10FE4`.

SharpOS-authored files are covered by the recorded owner grant/upstream CC0 evidence. The terminal engine under SharpOS `vendor/XtermSharp` is a separate MIT work, license SHA-256 `9AE8FA2FB06793CEDEA3E8E934275543B2452D8A03E5805D394FE2998CF3119`, with multiple upstream copyright notices. Do not copy that vendor tree under the SharpOS CC0 grant. Any later direct reuse requires a separate license/provenance review, retained notices, source firewall isolation, and an explicit decision that the engine fits CLROS.

Minimum excerpts identifying the two critical semantics:

```csharp
if (!e.IsManualReset) e.IsSet = false;
```

```csharp
if (!Enter()) return;
s_terminal.Feed(s_encode, length);
```

## Dependencies

- #189/M09-007 manual-reset and auto-reset events.
- #190/M09-008 semaphore/mutex ownership/wakeup rules.
- #196/M09-014 live `OSHost_*` logging.
- #199/M09-017 exported thread and wait/event functions.
- #210/M09-028 hosted allocation/thread/wait/timer smoke before any hosted console claim.
- #315 and #316 remain later optional packaging/PowerShell proof; this issue does not satisfy them.

## Exact host-leaf owned paths

- `src/OS.Kernel/PAL/OSHostConsoleInputContract.cs`
- `src/OS.Kernel/PAL/OSHostConsoleWaitContract.cs`
- `src/OS.Kernel/Diagnostics/SerializedTerminalFeed.cs`
- `tests/OS.HostTests/OSHostConsoleInputContractTests.cs`
- `tests/OS.HostTests/OSHostConsoleWaitContractTests.cs`
- `tests/OS.HostTests/SerializedTerminalFeedTests.cs`
- `docs/pal.md`
- `docs/security.md`
- exactly one new `done/stepNN.md`, reserved only after implementation/evidence exist

## Read-only and forbidden paths

Read-only: current `OSHost_*` status/table/facade contracts, wait/event/thread plans, app logging contracts, workload profiles, completion gates, license audit, and upstream sources.

Forbidden to the host leaf: `BootSequence.cs`, `Probes.cs`, `EfiEntry.cs`, `OS.csproj`, actual PAL export tables, shared QEMU/build scripts, keyboard/framebuffer drivers, app packages, references, vendor trees, generated artifacts, README, completion-gate promotion, and previous done steps. No `SharpOSHost_*` first-party symbol may be introduced.

## CLROS implementation contract

```csharp
public readonly struct OSHostConsoleKeyEvent
{
    public uint UnicodeScalar { get; }
    public ushort VirtualKey { get; }
    public OSHostConsoleModifiers Modifiers { get; }
    public bool KeyDown { get; }
    public bool IsRepeat { get; }
}

public static OSHostStatus TryReadConsoleEvent(
    ref OSHostConsoleInputState state,
    Span<OSHostConsoleKeyEvent> destination,
    out uint eventsWritten);

public static OSHostWaitResult PollAndConsume(
    ref OSHostWaitableState waitable,
    OSHostWaitMode mode,
    ulong deadlineTicks);
```

Required behavior:

1. Use canonical `OSHost_*` POD/status names, explicit lengths, opaque handles, and no managed references/exceptions across the ABI. `SharpOSHost_*` is reference-only.
2. Define deterministic key-down/up, repeat, Unicode scalar, modifier, navigation, Tab, Backspace, Delete, Home, End, PageUp/PageDown, Escape, and Enter translation. Invalid/incomplete extended scan sequences fail without corrupting the queue.
3. Use a fixed-capacity caller-owned ring with exact overflow policy and counters. Never silently report a dropped key as accepted.
4. A successful zero-timeout poll of an auto-reset event consumes the signal exactly once. A manual-reset event stays signaled. A successful semaphore poll consumes exactly one count. Wait-any returns the correct index and cannot spin forever on an unconsumed signal.
5. Deadline arithmetic is monotonic/checked. Cover timeout zero, finite deadline, infinite policy where allowed, cancellation, stale/invalid handles, abandoned mutex state, and capacity exhaustion.
6. Serialize terminal parser feeds with explicit ownership. Input bytes may not be dropped or interleaved. Rendering may be coalesced/skipped under an explicit bounded policy; parser state may not.
7. Parser/feed input has watchdog, byte budget, operation budget, bounded screen dimensions, checked cursor/range arithmetic, and no throw/hang behavior for arbitrary byte corpora.
8. This host leaf does not select or vendor XtermSharp, draw a framebuffer, open a shell, start PowerShell, or expose remote administration.

## Host evidence

Tests must include event/semaphore consumption on zero-timeout polls, wait-any ordering, manual-reset persistence, finite timeout, invalid handles, queue wrap/overflow, all named key translations, incomplete extended keys, concurrent feed serialization, dropped-render-not-dropped-input, arbitrary byte corpora, watchdog, deterministic final state, and warmed allocation checks.

```text
TEST_START m09.console-terminal
CLROS_M09_CONSOLE_TERMINAL_READY autoResetPollConsumes=true feedSerialized=true parserBounded=true hostOnly=true
TEST_PASS m09.console-terminal
```

## Real-QEMU integration

Before closure, a separately claimed opt-in QEMU profile must link the reviewed contracts into the no-stdlib/hosted boundary, inject a deterministic synthetic key/event sequence, run two concurrent writers through the serialized feed, exercise zero-timeout wait-any consumption, and observe exactly one:

```text
CLROS_M09_CONSOLE_TERMINAL_READY autoResetPollConsumes=true feedSerialized=true parserBounded=true guestIntegrated=true
CONSOLE_TERMINAL_CONTRACT_FAILED
```

Fresh real QEMU/OVMF must use exact source/artifact hashes, forbid the issue failure and every `TEST_FAIL`, and preserve serial/QEMU summaries. Synthetic guest proof is not PSReadLine or physical keyboard proof. #316 later must prove the actual pinned PowerShell/PSReadLine behavior while preserving no SSH/login/remote-admin defaults.

## Documentation, acceptance, and boundary

Update `docs/pal.md` and `docs/security.md` with ABI shape, queue/wait/feed rules, optional-profile status, unsupported UI/device behavior, and evidence. Reserve one unique done step; run focused/full host gates, naming/source firewall, QEMU profile, ownership audit, and independent exact-head review.

Acceptance proves only the bounded console/wait/feed contracts and their synthetic guest profile. It does not prove XtermSharp adoption, full VT/xterm compatibility, physical keyboard/framebuffer behavior, PowerShell, a login shell, SSH, hosted .NET completeness, Kestrel, provider support, CloudReady status, production readiness, or a completion-gate advance.

<!-- clros-canonical-review:2026-10-23 -->
## Current implementation requirements (2026-10-23)

- Zero-timeout polling must consume auto-reset/semaphore state exactly once, while manual reset remains signaled. Define cancellation/close races and serialized bounded feed; do not inherit cooperative/global reference assumptions or expand into a default shell.

- Reference: https://github.com/daniilvaino/SharpOS/blob/b80ee3a4175e1522d1a12ba7fe371a49da3207f5/OS/src/Kernel/Threading/Event.cs#L3-L93. Wait/Set show manual-reset versus one-signal auto-reset behavior, but explicitly assume cooperative single-CPU serialization and a LIFO queue. Add atomic predicate/enqueue/park and cancellation/timeout tests for CLROS preemption. SHA-256 `4b9d50a917d71fbd84c2bb0aae28e9f8af86092d9175dc908d68750a9c6f31da`. CC0 for SharpOS-authored source; vendor terms remain separate.

- Reference: https://github.com/daniilvaino/SharpOS/blob/b80ee3a4175e1522d1a12ba7fe371a49da3207f5/OS/src/Kernel/Threading/Semaphore.cs#L28-L86. Wait/Release hand permits directly to waiting threads; surplus Count is clamped to Max. CLROS must specify overflow/release errors and ownership rather than silently importing the clamp or cooperative scheduling assumptions. SHA-256 `5466ebeb078b114afa77c6143d60f785dc6867b7fe9c05b99a733ba5fe05fff4`. CC0 for SharpOS-authored source; vendor terms remain separate.

supplementalIssues.title: [Future optional] Parse and validate exFAT boot regions without mounting or writing
supplementalIssues.body:
<!-- clros-supplemental-scope:future-exfat-boot-region-parser -->
## Goal and priority

Future optional storage research: implement only a bounded, read-only exFAT boot-region/geometry parser and independent hostile-input tests. This could later enable removable/data-volume access, but FAT32/virtio-blk remains the primary appliance path. This is not a request for a complete exFAT filesystem or exFAT writes.

Keep `agent:blocked`, `priority:p3`. Dependencies #122, #126 and #127 must be accepted before scheduling this optional work. The issue is supplemental, outside `.gitea/backlog/clros-issues.json`, and intentionally has no milestone assignment; it must not become a prerequisite for the current M06 exit, NativeAOT, .NET or Kestrel work. Labels identify its subsystem phase, not a changed gate.

The 2026-10-06 all-state review found no existing exFAT issue. RedPandaOS lists exFAT in its roadmap but has no exFAT implementation at `3a2e08183847d4d9596fcfe1cd853474313c45b4`. Use the maintained DiscUtils fork for this reference.

## Read first and pinned references

Read `AGENTS.md`, `docs/documentation-map.md`, `docs/cstorage.md`, `docs/image-builder.md`, `docs/license-audit.md`, `docs/reference-map.md`, `docs/completion-gates.md`, the local kernel/shared/test guides, and `src/OS.Kernel/Storage/Fat32Parser.cs` plus `tests/OS.HostTests/StorageFat32ParserTests.cs` for existing status/test conventions.

- [`references/DiscUtils-96e8f6bc4d8d/Library/DiscUtils.ExFat/Internal/Partition/ExFatBootSector.cs`](https://github.com/LTRData/DiscUtils/blob/96e8f6bc4d8daa0da84e07556f5623c1e79a34a2/Library/DiscUtils.ExFat/Internal/Partition/ExFatBootSector.cs): field offsets, main-region checksum and excluded mutable bytes; validate lengths/shifts before translating the algorithm.
- [`references/DiscUtils-96e8f6bc4d8d/Tests/LibraryTests/ExFat/Tests/PartitionStructureTests.cs`](https://github.com/LTRData/DiscUtils/blob/96e8f6bc4d8daa0da84e07556f5623c1e79a34a2/Tests/LibraryTests/ExFat/Tests/PartitionStructureTests.cs): host fixture structure and geometry scenarios; author tiny fixtures independently.
- [`references/DiscUtils-96e8f6bc4d8d/Library/DiscUtils.ExFat/Internal/Partition/ExFatAllocationBitmap.cs`](https://github.com/LTRData/DiscUtils/blob/96e8f6bc4d8daa0da84e07556f5623c1e79a34a2/Library/DiscUtils.ExFat/Internal/Partition/ExFatAllocationBitmap.cs) and [`references/DiscUtils-96e8f6bc4d8d/Library/DiscUtils.ExFat/Internal/Partition/ExFatUpCaseTable.cs`](https://github.com/LTRData/DiscUtils/blob/96e8f6bc4d8daa0da84e07556f5623c1e79a34a2/Library/DiscUtils.ExFat/Internal/Partition/ExFatUpCaseTable.cs): later-feature reading only, outside this issue.
- [Microsoft exFAT specification](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/exfat-specification): normative layout/checksum authority. DiscUtils MIT/ExFat picrap attribution is preserved in the snapshot; no code/fixture asset import is authorized by this issue's test-only disposition.

## Exact proposed owned paths

- `src/OS.Kernel/Storage/ExFatBootRegionParser.cs`
- `src/OS.Kernel/Storage/ExFatVolumeGeometry.cs`
- `std/no-runtime/shared/Hash/ExFatBootChecksum.cs`
- `tests/OS.HostTests/StorageExFatBootRegionTests.cs`
- `docs/cstorage.md`
- one newly reserved `done/stepNN.md`

These source paths are proposed, not existing implementation. Existing `IReadOnlyBlockDevice`, `BlockDeviceInfo`, endian helpers and FAT contracts are read-only inputs.

## Small implementation slice

1. Parse caller-provided boot-region bytes against explicit partition start, device block size and block count. Return a POD geometry/status result and no pointers into mutable caller data. The first slice performs no device I/O.
2. Validate minimum input, signatures/revision, reserved fields, sector/cluster shift ranges before shifting, FAT count/policy, FAT and cluster-heap extents, root cluster, volume/device bounds and every conversion/add/multiply. Document supported single-FAT exFAT; return an explicit unsupported result for TexFAT or unsupported revisions.
3. Verify the complete main boot-region checksum, including every repeated checksum word. The rotate/add checksum intentionally uses 32-bit wrap, distinct from checked geometry arithmetic; bytes 106, 107 and 112 are excluded according to the specification.
4. If backup bytes are supplied, validate that boot region independently and report main/backup validity and immutable geometry agreement. Do not silently repair media or select a conflicting copy. Invalid main with valid backup yields an explicit recovery-needed status, not automatic mount success.
5. Unsupported/truncated/overflowing input returns deterministic failure with a default/unusable result. Check lengths before reads; no scan proportional to attacker-supplied cluster counts and no heap allocation.

## Acceptance cases

Hand-author valid 512-byte and 4096-byte sector boot regions plus exact-boundary variants. Cover short input at every fixed header/checksum boundary, invalid shift, zero/overflowed geometry, overlapping FAT/heap, root out of range, device-bound overflow, one bad repeated checksum word, one changed protected byte, allowed mutable-byte changes, both copies valid, invalid main/valid backup, conflicting valid copies, unsupported revision/two-FAT policy and unchanged input bytes on every path. Warmed allocation checks cover the parser, not fixture construction.

```text
TEST_START storage.exfat.boot-region
CLROS_EXFAT_BOOT_REGION_READY hostOnly=true readOnly=true mount=false
TEST_PASS storage.exfat.boot-region
TEST_FAIL storage.exfat.boot-region <reason>
```

## Validation and evidence

Use C# 14/.NET 11, explicit status/results, checked extents and caller-owned buffers. Shared binary/checksum primitives belong under `std/no-runtime/shared` before kernel use. No exceptions, hidden allocation, reflection or dynamic invocation on the kernel path. Register the new test class using the existing HostTests explicit [HostTest] discovery convention; do not merely compile an uncalled test method.

Run from `C:\Projects\CLROS`:

```powershell
dotnet build .\CLROS.slnx --nologo -m:1
dotnet build .\tests\OS.HostTests\OS.HostTests.csproj --nologo
dotnet run --project .\tests\OS.HostTests\OS.HostTests.csproj --no-build
Use compiled `dotnet run --project tools/OS.Tooling -- repo check` and `contracts check`; reserve evidence with `done reserve`.
git diff --check
git status --short
```

Capture exit codes, complete logs, exactly one scoped start/pass envelope, no scoped failure and the terminal `TEST_PASS host.tests`. Reserve a new done step with `scripts/new-done-step.ps1 -Reserve`; preserve commands, source/artifact hashes, failures, deferred work and the host-only boundary. Update the named subsystem doc with supported and rejected inputs, not a completion-gate claim. Post evidence before closure.

Forbidden changes: boot ordering/EFI linkage, probe toggles, PAL ABI, apps, upstream snapshots, existing done steps, completion gates and the managed backlog manifest. Any later live integration needs a separately scoped issue and the proper collision lane.

## Deferred work and boundary

Directory entry sets/checksums, allocation bitmap, upcase/name hashing, NoFatChain contiguous extents, file reads, dirty-volume recovery, mount integration and all writes are deferred. This issue proves only host parsing/checksum behavior. It does not prove firmware boot support, a mounted filesystem, live storage, removable hardware, crash recovery or a CLROS completion gate.

supplementalIssues.body:
<!-- clros-supplemental-scope:future-owned-framebuffer-surface -->
## Goal and priority

Future optional diagnostics: add a bounded caller-owned framebuffer surface and tiny monochrome glyph blit for local failure visibility. Keep owned serial as the primary machine-readable evidence channel. This first slice is host-only and performs no port I/O, MMIO mapping, mode setting or firmware calls.

Keep `agent:blocked`, `priority:p3` until #65 (firmware adapter invalidation) and #94 (owned physical mapping/cache policy) are accepted. This supplemental issue has no milestone assignment and is outside `.gitea/backlog/clros-issues.json`; it is not a new M05/Kestrel prerequisite. The all-state review found #65 owns metadata/adapter lifetime, #94 owns mapping/cache policy, and #470 owns optional console input/feed semantics and explicitly excludes framebuffer drawing. Historical paging/reservation issues and their epics also do not implement a pixel renderer. Do not duplicate or extend those scopes here.

## Read first and pinned references

Read `AGENTS.md`, `docs/documentation-map.md`, `docs/drivers.md`, `docs/diagnostics.md`, `docs/boot-order.md`, `docs/license-audit.md`, `docs/completion-gates.md`, and local kernel/test guides. Existing read-only inputs are `src/OS.Kernel/Platform/IPlatformFramebuffer.cs`, `GuardedPlatformFramebuffer.cs`, `tests/OS.HostTests/PlatformFramebufferGuardTests.cs`, plus shared endian and buffer helpers.

- [`references/RedPandaOS-3a2e08183847/RedPandaOS/Kernel/Devices/VGA.cs`](https://github.com/giawa/RedPandaOS/blob/3a2e08183847d4d9596fcfe1cd853474313c45b4/RedPandaOS/Kernel/Devices/VGA.cs): text-cell/cursor behavior and negative coordinate cases; fixed 0xB8000 and 80x25 are not a portable framebuffer contract.
- [`references/RedPandaOS-3a2e08183847/RedPandaOS/Kernel/Devices/BGA.cs`](https://github.com/giawa/RedPandaOS/blob/3a2e08183847d4d9596fcfe1cd853474313c45b4/RedPandaOS/Kernel/Devices/BGA.cs): concrete Bochs register/mode/y-offset example for a possible later backend. Its 32-bit BAR heuristic and weak mode/aperture bounds must not be copied.
- [`references/RedPandaOS-3a2e08183847/RedPandaOS/Kernel/BitmapFont.cs`](https://github.com/giawa/RedPandaOS/blob/3a2e08183847d4d9596fcfe1cd853474313c45b4/RedPandaOS/Kernel/BitmapFont.cs): glyph metrics, signed offsets and clipping scenarios. Use independently authored test glyph bytes; bundled Inconsolata assets have separate OFL terms.

RedPandaOS source is MIT with separate font terms; preserve attribution if a later issue deliberately adapts eligible source. This issue derives behavior/tests independently and imports no font assets.

## Exact proposed owned paths

- `src/OS.Kernel/Platform/OwnedFramebufferSurface.cs`
- `src/OS.Kernel/Diagnostics/FramebufferGlyphBlitter.cs`
- `tests/OS.HostTests/OwnedFramebufferSurfaceTests.cs`
- `tests/OS.HostTests/FramebufferGlyphBlitterTests.cs`
- `docs/drivers.md`
- `docs/diagnostics.md`
- one newly reserved `done/stepNN.md`

## Small implementation slice

1. Accept already-copied framebuffer metadata and a caller-owned byte span. Retain existing `PlatformFramebufferMetadata` vocabulary; do not recapture firmware state. Validate width, height, stride, byte extent and RGBX/BGRX format before creating a usable surface. Reject Bitmask/BltOnly/unknown formats initially.
2. Translate pixel positions to byte offsets with explicit checked arithmetic. Keep row padding and every byte beyond the declared surface unchanged. Reject overlapping source/destination buffers or define and test a safe policy before writing.
3. Blit a caller-provided fixed monochrome glyph using explicit source stride/extent, signed origin and foreground color. Clip deliberately at each edge without unsigned wrap; malformed geometry must fail before any mutation. Use fixed integer operations and no font parser, text layout, allocation, exceptions or string formatting.
4. A failed glyph operation returns status and leaves the destination unchanged. A valid fully clipped glyph is a deterministic no-op. Serial logging remains independent; renderer failures cannot recursively invoke the renderer.

## Acceptance cases

Cover RGBX/BGRX expected bytes, nontrivial row padding, all four clipping edges, negative glyph origin, glyph larger than surface, fully clipped/zero-sized request, extent exactly sufficient/one byte short, arithmetic overflow, invalid metadata/pixel format, overlapping spans, unchanged row-padding/tail canaries and warmed zero-allocation behavior. Use a tiny independently authored asymmetric test glyph so mirroring/bit-order errors are visible in byte assertions.

```text
TEST_START diagnostics.framebuffer.surface
CLROS_FRAMEBUFFER_SURFACE_READY hostOnly=true firmwareCalls=false deviceIo=false
TEST_PASS diagnostics.framebuffer.surface
TEST_FAIL diagnostics.framebuffer.surface <reason>
```

## Validation and evidence

Use C# 14/.NET 11, explicit status/results, checked extents and caller-owned buffers. Shared binary/checksum primitives belong under `std/no-runtime/shared` before kernel use. No exceptions, hidden allocation, reflection or dynamic invocation on the kernel path. Register the new test class using the existing HostTests explicit [HostTest] discovery convention; do not merely compile an uncalled test method.

Run from `C:\Projects\CLROS`:

```powershell
dotnet build .\CLROS.slnx --nologo -m:1
dotnet build .\tests\OS.HostTests\OS.HostTests.csproj --nologo
dotnet run --project .\tests\OS.HostTests\OS.HostTests.csproj --no-build
Use compiled `dotnet run --project tools/OS.Tooling -- repo check` and `contracts check`; reserve evidence with `done reserve`.
git diff --check
git status --short
```

Capture exit codes, complete logs, exactly one scoped start/pass envelope, no scoped failure and the terminal `TEST_PASS host.tests`. Reserve a new done step with `scripts/new-done-step.ps1 -Reserve`; preserve commands, source/artifact hashes, failures, deferred work and the host-only boundary. Update the named subsystem doc with supported and rejected inputs, not a completion-gate claim. Post evidence before closure.

Forbidden changes: boot ordering/EFI linkage, probe toggles, PAL ABI, apps, upstream snapshots, existing done steps, completion gates and the managed backlog manifest. Any later live integration needs a separately scoped issue and the proper collision lane.

## Deferred work and boundary

A later optional backend could map a copied GOP framebuffer or implement a bounded QEMU Bochs BGA backend after PCI/BAR ownership and cache-policy prerequisites. It needs its own live guest evidence. VGA text mode, BGA modes, fonts/text consoles, scrolling, virtio-GPU, compositors, GUI, input and remote desktop are outside this issue. No default shell/admin surface is added. Host pixel tests are not display hardware or post-EBS proof.

supplementalIssues.body:
<!-- clros-supplemental-scope:uacpi-gas-metadata -->
## Goal and readiness

Add one host-qualified, pure C# decoder and register-metadata validator for the 12-byte ACPI Generic Address Structure (GAS). `agent:ready`, `priority:p3`; no implementation dependency is open. This does not authorize a new live register-access path.

Read first: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/documentation-map.md`, `docs/host-requirements.md`, `docs/drivers.md`, `docs/reference-map.md`, `docs/fork-diff.md`, `docs/license-audit.md`, `docs/completion-gates.md`, and the applicable directory-local guides.

Pinned reference: `references/uACPI-2cb5e71ef583`, upstream [uACPI](https://github.com/uACPI/uACPI), commit `2cb5e71ef58393839e1988ef9a8f1d8ba2845a8d` (6.1.1). All 168 installed files match their original Git blobs. The isolated snapshot is ignored and is never a first-party build input. The project library carries the MIT license; independently author C# and fixtures, preserving provenance/notices if future substantial adaptation occurs.

This is supplemental optional work outside `.gitea/backlog/clros-issues.json`, with no milestone assignment or new prerequisite for existing M05/Kestrel acceptance. Leave it unassigned until deliberately claimed. Finish currently owned work first.

## Owned files and interface

- New `src/OS.Kernel/Boot/AcpiGenericAddress.cs`.
- New `tests/OS.HostTests/AcpiGenericAddressTests.cs`.
- `docs/drivers.md` for the bounded contract and a newly reserved done step.
- Expose `AcpiGenericAddress.Parse(ReadOnlySpan<byte>)` with readonly raw metadata/status, plus `ValidateRegister(...)` for a supported SystemMemory/SystemIO register description. Keep raw decoding separate from register-access policy. Preserve the original address-space, bit width, bit offset and encoded access-size fields. Consume exactly 12 bytes from a sufficiently sized input.

## Behavior and independent cases

- Decode the little-endian 64-bit address without host structure packing or pointer dereference.
- Access-size encodings 1/2/3/4 denote 8/16/32/64 bits. Encoding 0 remains unspecified metadata and requires caller policy before access; do not silently invent an access width.
- Register validation rejects unsupported address spaces, reserved access-size encodings, zero address, zero/register widths above 64, offset plus width above 64, unsupported 64-bit SystemIO access, and address-range overflow when an explicit access width is available.
- Cover all four encoded sizes, every truncated source length below 12, high addresses, field-boundary arithmetic, nonzero offsets, unknown spaces, and unchanged input bytes on both success and failure.
- Do not implement MMIO/port I/O, mapping, barriers, read-modify-write, PCI reset, HPET changes or fallback hardware access.

## Reference observations

Study [`include/uacpi/acpi.h`](https://github.com/uACPI/uACPI/blob/2cb5e71ef58393839e1988ef9a8f1d8ba2845a8d/include/uacpi/acpi.h) and [`source/io.c`](https://github.com/uACPI/uACPI/blob/2cb5e71ef58393839e1988ef9a8f1d8ba2845a8d/source/io.c) (`gas_get_access_bit_width`, `gas_validate`, `uacpi_map_gas_noalloc`). Original `source/io.c` SHA-256: `3fedf3e5cccdcac67eb82bc9a66f7a86cf399256cebdc774b3605a358b882731`.

A static concern in the nonzero-offset/access-size branch multiplies the encoded value by eight: encodings 3/4 yield 24/32, unlike the specification's 32/64. This is a source observation, not an executed upstream defect. The authoritative [ACPI 6.6 GAS table](https://uefi.org/specs/ACPI/6.6/05_ACPI_Software_Programming_Model.html#generic-address-structure) must define independent fixtures; reference round-trip agreement is not an oracle.

## Acceptance and commands

- Register independent deterministic cases in the normal explicit host-test inventory using `[HostTest(..., HostLane.Fast, ...)]`; no explicit [HostTest] discovery or subset projects.
- Run `dotnet build tests/OS.HostTests/OS.HostTests.csproj --nologo`, then `dotnet run --project tests/OS.HostTests --no-build -- --filter AcpiGenericAddressTests`.
- Expected fixture records: `TEST_START acpi.gas <case>`, `TEST_PASS acpi.gas <case>`, and `TEST_FAIL acpi.gas <case> <reason>` for failure reporting. A filtered run is not full-host acceptance.
- Run `dotnet run --project tools/OS.Tooling -- repo check`, `dotnet run --project tools/OS.Tooling -- contracts check`, and `git diff --check`.
- Update `docs/drivers.md`; reserve a new step with `dotnet run --project tools/OS.Tooling -- done reserve`, record commands, results, failures and evidence boundary, and post/read back evidence before closure.
- First-party source is C# 14/.NET 11, allocation-free on kernel-facing paths, with span inputs, explicit lengths, POD/status results, no exceptions, reflection, hidden allocation or hardware side effects. Cover warmed zero-allocation and reference-free result metadata.
- Do not modify `src/OS/**`, `BootSequence.cs`, `Diagnostics/Probes.cs`, the solution, first-party project/build inputs, reference snapshot files or completion-gate status. A later native/guest integration requires separately owned issues.

## Evidence boundary

Only raw decoding and host-tested register metadata are in scope. No physical mapping, register operation, FADT retention, native/guest execution, general ACPI/AML, Gate 6, hosted .NET/Kestrel, cloud or production claim.

- Validate the entire input and required descriptor count before writing caller-owned output; EndTag is termination metadata and does not occupy a resource descriptor. Destination exhaustion returns required capacity and leaves the output unchanged.
- Cover EndTag-only input, mixed small/large descriptors, opaque items, every truncated header shape, payload length overrun, missing/malformed EndTag, both checksum modes, trailing bytes, exact capacity and one-short capacity. supplementalIssues.title: [Future ACPI research] Design a bounded C# AML path for device/resource discovery
supplementalIssues.body:
<!-- clros-supplemental-scope:uacpi-csharp-aml-research -->
## Goal and research readiness

Research a staged, C# 14/.NET 11 AML/device-discovery path compatible with CLROS's retained ownership and status contracts. Scheduling review on 2026-10-12 verified #662/#663/#664 qualified in `done/step1187.md`, merged and closed with `agent:done`. This issue is now `agent:ready`, `priority:p3`, unassigned, for source/design research only. The former #658/#659/#660 dependency is also qualified/closed in `done/step1184.md`. Real AML hardware execution still requires the stronger runtime and owned-service dependencies below.

Read first: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/documentation-map.md`, `docs/host-requirements.md`, `docs/drivers.md`, `docs/reference-map.md`, `docs/fork-diff.md`, `docs/license-audit.md`, `docs/completion-gates.md`, and the applicable directory-local guides.

Pinned reference: `references/uACPI-2cb5e71ef583`, upstream [uACPI](https://github.com/uACPI/uACPI), commit `2cb5e71ef58393839e1988ef9a8f1d8ba2845a8d` (6.1.1). All 168 installed files match their original Git blobs. The isolated snapshot is ignored and is never a first-party build input. The project library carries the MIT license; independently author C# and fixtures, preserving provenance/notices if future substantial adaptation occurs.

This is supplemental optional work outside `.gitea/backlog/clros-issues.json`, with no milestone assignment or new prerequisite for existing M05/Kestrel acceptance. Leave it unassigned until deliberately claimed. Finish currently owned work first.

## Owned files and deliverable

- `docs/drivers.md` for the future ACPI/AML staging and dependency matrix.
- `docs/fork-diff.md` for pinned reference comparisons and rejection cases.
- A newly reserved done step.
- Produce a decision-complete research design and small proposed follow-ups; this issue implements no interpreter, PAL ABI or live device path. Recheck existing all-state issues before proposing follow-ups.
- Cross-reference #665, #666 and #667 as optional host foundations; their completion is not necessary to begin this source/design research.

## Required research

- Define a minimal first host experiment: explicitly owned immutable AML bytes, bounded namespace/object storage, one no-I/O integer method, status-coded evaluation and invalid-opcode/package/name/bounds rejection.
- Compare uACPI's explicit interpreter call frames/opcode programs, non-recursive object teardown, namespace lookup and reference semantics against no-stdlib/NativeAOT limitations. Specify call-depth, instruction, allocation/namespace and elapsed-time budgets; loop timeout alone does not bound all work.
- Stage future `_STA` device status, `_CRS` resource buffers and `_PRT` routing separately. Plan DSDT/SSDT retention before firmware exit and explicit operation-region capabilities; table discovery alone supplies no access authority.
- Map real runtime implementation dependencies to existing #188 (thread lifecycle), #189 (events), #190 (mutex/semaphore), #194 (work queues), #198 (time/sleep), owned mappings and controller/IRQ services. Distinguish research readiness from the stronger prerequisites for real AML hardware execution.
- Start with operation-region I/O and writes disabled. Plan negative cases for forbidden SystemMemory/SystemIO/PCI requests, failed allocation/registration, budget exhaustion, incomplete cleanup and stale references.
- Review upstream PR #166 independently, retaining its reviewed head `e60f36fe89e020a50a847fe1f7c1a47af1d81731` separately from the installed master pin. It proposes lifetime/reference-cycle, event/notify deadlock and kernel callback changes. Include independent tests for these failure classes; do not assume unmerged code is accepted.
- Defer SCI/GPE, embedded controllers, hotplug, suspend/resume and full AML compatibility to separate later issues. No C library linking or wholesale subsystem port.

## Pinned source loci

- [`source/interpreter.c`](https://github.com/uACPI/uACPI/blob/2cb5e71ef58393839e1988ef9a8f1d8ba2845a8d/source/interpreter.c); SHA-256 `028e5c88ef4bec83f9af692f3a4aae6805352f4fd1b9883c27f050f7171df528`.
- [`source/types.c`](https://github.com/uACPI/uACPI/blob/2cb5e71ef58393839e1988ef9a8f1d8ba2845a8d/source/types.c), `source/shareable.c`, `source/namespace.c`, `source/opregion.c`, `source/default_handlers.c`, `source/event.c`, `source/notify.c` and `include/uacpi/kernel_api.h`.
- `tests/test-cases/hanging-while.asl`, `infinite-recursion.asl`, `pci-regions-track-bridges.asl` and `tests/runner/interface_impl.c` are source/test-design references.
- [Upstream PR #166](https://github.com/uACPI/uACPI/pull/166) and [ACPI 6.6 specification](https://uefi.org/specs/ACPI/6.6/) supply separate review context.

## Acceptance and commands

- Deliver a source-backed API/data-flow outline, dependency/authority matrix, bounded first experiment, negative controls and staged host/native/guest acceptance; each runtime gap is mapped to an existing issue or a small justified proposal.
- Run `dotnet run --project tools/OS.Tooling -- repo check`, `dotnet run --project tools/OS.Tooling -- contracts check`, and `git diff --check`. Expected checks include `TEST_PASS naming.guard`, `TEST_PASS source.firewall` and the existing successful contract audit records.
- Reserve a new step with `dotnet run --project tools/OS.Tooling -- done reserve`; record review commands, exact reference pins/hashes, limitations and deferred work; post/read back the research evidence before closing.
- Do not run downloaded reference bootstrap/test scripts or import hardware ACPI dumps automatically. Any later differential experiment needs a separately authorized, pinned host-only setup outside `references/`.

## Evidence boundary

This issue produces research and follow-up designs only. It changes no public runtime interface, compiler/EH behavior, boot order, probe defaults, native image or gate status. General AML, live device/resource discovery, Gate 6, hosted .NET/Kestrel, cloud and production remain unqualified.
