supplementalIssues.title: Compare a custom Kestrel byte-stream transport with the pinned Linux socket payload (host only)
supplementalIssues.body:
<!-- clros-research:kestrel-transport-20261012 -->
## Coordination

- Supplemental research issue; no managed issue key, formal milestone or managed parent.
- Labels: `agent:ready`, `priority:p1`, `type:research`, `evidence:host`, `component:app-model`, `phase:m16-nativeaot`.
- Evidence prerequisite: qualified [M16-001 / #679](http://192.168.4.35:3000/admin/CLROS/issues/679), `done/step1198.md`. Related foundation: [#678](http://192.168.4.35:3000/admin/CLROS/issues/678).
- This experiment is not a dependency of #684, #685, M16 socket/epoll implementation, M10 Kestrel acceptance or foundation closure. The stock Linux ABI route remains primary unless a later architecture decision changes it.

## Objective and scope

Determine whether replacing only Kestrel's socket transport with an application-side C# byte-stream adapter materially reduces CLROS platform work while preserving the actual Kestrel HTTP engine and Minimal API pipeline. Compare a measured prototype; a new interface design alone is insufficient.

Use the M16-001 SDK10.0.401/Core+ASP.NET+ILC10.0.12/musl1.2.6 pins, `linux-musl-x64`, static non-PIE, invariant globalization, workstation GC, HTTP/1.1 and the same `MinimalApiSmoke` application/configuration. Rebuild both variants from one frozen source tree; the candidate's only intentional application difference is transport registration. Record the source delta and distinct binary hashes. Preserve baseline behavior and make the study opt-in.

Implement `IConnectionListenerFactory`/`IConnectionListener` and `ConnectionContext.Transport` using bounded paired `IDuplexPipe` instances. Retain the upstream Kestrel server, parser, middleware and routing. A bounded host byte-stream backend stands in for a possible future CLROS service; explicitly document which accept/read/write/close/cancel operations it requires. Do not change `OSHost_*`, invent a kernel ABI or add kernel exports in this slice.

`UseKestrelCore()` registers sockets in the pinned version. After builder defaults, explicitly remove the stock `IConnectionListenerFactory` registrations and install the candidate; assert which factory creates the listener so both variants cannot accidentally exercise sockets. Inspect [WebHostBuilderKestrelExtensions.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v10.0.12/src/Servers/Kestrel/Kestrel/src/WebHostBuilderKestrelExtensions.cs) and [TransportManager.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v10.0.12/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Infrastructure/TransportManager.cs). Managed `System.IO.Pipelines` buffers are not POSIX pipe descriptors. Preserve/trace the existing host lifetime and logging settings; changing ConsoleLifetime to remove signal services is a separate measured variant, never an assumed side effect of transport replacement.

Run matching request bytes through the baseline socket transport and candidate transport. An in-memory driver is sufficient for transport semantics, but is not external TCP evidence. If a host TCP bridge is used, identify and trace its process/backend separately; moving a syscall into the bridge is not removing the underlying service requirement.

## Source and file scope

- Read `docs/workload-profiles.md`, `docs/kestrel.md`, `docs/networking.md`, `docs/nativeaot-nostdlib-limits.md`, `done/step1198.md` and applicable agent guides first.
- Reuse `apps/MinimalApiSmoke/Program.cs`, its project and `tools/OS.Tooling/NativeAotPayload.cs` pin/ELF/provenance conventions. Permit only a small opt-in transport hook in the baseline app; place study types in `apps/MinimalApiSmoke/TransportStudy/` and a compiled driver in proposed `tools/OS.KestrelTransportStudy/`.
- Keep one main public type per file. First-party code is C#14/.NET11. No EFI/kernel/profile changes, native shim source, reference imports or edits to historical evidence.
- Inspect live claims before touching the shared MinimalApiSmoke app; coordinate with #214/#215 owners. Prefer an isolated study build with a documented source delta when concurrent work owns that app. This research issue grants no shared kernel integration lane.
- Read pinned ASP.NET v10.0.12 MIT sources: [IConnectionListenerFactory.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v10.0.12/src/Servers/Connections.Abstractions/src/IConnectionListenerFactory.cs), [IConnectionListener.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v10.0.12/src/Servers/Connections.Abstractions/src/IConnectionListener.cs), [ConnectionContext.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v10.0.12/src/Servers/Connections.Abstractions/src/ConnectionContext.cs), and [SocketTransportFactory.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v10.0.12/src/Servers/Kestrel/Transport.Sockets/src/SocketTransportFactory.cs). Resolve/tag-pin and hash consulted source in the report before adaptation.

## Acceptance

1. Both final-source static NativeAOT variants pass ELF inspection and execute the same real Kestrel `/healthz` endpoint, yielding HTTP200 and exact `OS_MINIMAL_API_OK`. Preserve configured-body/config checks so the report attributes the response to the intended app rather than an unrelated listener. Retain baseline external-HTTP proof; label the candidate's actual I/O path precisely.
2. Exercise fragmented request headers, repeated keep-alive and concurrent connections, a slow reader that forces bounded-pipe backpressure, input EOF, abort/reset, cancelled accept/read/write, malformed HTTP, and shutdown with active/pending operations. Check no deadlock, cross-connection bytes, lingering owned task/handle or unbounded buffer growth. Record unsupported cases; no successful no-op behavior.
3. Under the same Linux builder/profile, retain separate `strace -ff` startup/request/idle/shutdown traces, thread counts, ELF/native dependencies, size and coarse allocation/memory observations. Classify baseline-only, candidate-only and common requirements, plus driver/bridge costs. Supplement traces with matched upstream error-path review; a syscall absent from one run is not proof it is unnecessary.
4. Explicitly report remaining upstream GC/EH, TLS, ThreadPool, timers, thread/signal/futex and memory requirements. A transport substitution alone establishes no removal of these services. Compare implementation/maintenance cost as well as observed syscall names; avoid benchmark claims from unequal I/O paths.
5. Deliver a source-backed adopt/defer/reject recommendation and a reproducible report in a new reserved `done/stepNN.md`, with commands, source/compiler/app/trace hashes and honest failure details. A measured negative result can close this research issue. Update the existing `docs/kestrel.md` research section without advancing guest gates or replacing the primary roadmap.

## Commands and markers

Checks after implementing the proposed project: `dotnet build tools/OS.KestrelTransportStudy --nologo`, `dotnet run --project tools/OS.Tooling -- repo check`, `dotnet run --project tools/OS.Tooling -- contracts check`, `git diff --check`.

Implement the proposed driver interface `dotnet run --project tools/OS.KestrelTransportStudy -- compare --output <fresh-directory>`; this interface does not exist yet. The driver must retain exact publish/trace argument arrays and fail visibly if the matched Linux builder/toolchain is unavailable. Use `TEST_START kestrel.transport.study`, `TEST_PASS kestrel.transport.study` and `TEST_FAIL kestrel.transport.study <reason>` for the study's checks. Do not emit `TEST_PASS kestrel.smoke`.

Boundary: host-only custom-transport feasibility. This does not prove live CLROS TCP, a production transport, CLROS Kestrel execution, process isolation, cloud readiness or elimination of runtime platform services.


<!-- clros-canonical-review:2026-10-23 -->
## Current implementation requirements (2026-10-23)

- The .NET10.0.12 baseline and permission to modify MinimalApiSmoke are stale for current work. Preserve the accepted fixture and use an isolated study app built against a deliberately pinned current .NET11 recipe; any historical .NET10 reproduction must be explicitly labeled. This optional custom transport cannot become a requirement for normal apps in #793-#797.

- Reference: https://github.com/Sadik00789/SharpMetal/blob/b29c452f7d6c8d8609d1a007b0b6ae8bdcc84807/src/kernel/Posix/PosixSyscallDispatch.cs#L41-L119. Dispatch obtains process state and returns -ENOSYS for unknown calls; its bounce buffers are global and SysRead accepts a null buffer as zero progress. Use these as negative concurrency/EFAULT tests, not a complete Linux ABI. SHA-256 `3c0c0964752de4c6240286b2385962a33b526ab4a7488420a0b368f5cd958c67`. MIT.

This description is maintained in `supplementalIssues` in `.gitea/backlog/clros-issues.json`; preserve its existing issue identity and human addenda. Reference inspection supplies test ideas, not CLROS acceptance.

supplementalIssues.title: Assess an optional .NET 11 WASI HTTP handler and custom ASP.NET IServer profile (host only)
supplementalIssues.body:
<!-- clros-research:wasi-http-20261012 -->
## Coordination

- Supplemental optional research issue; no managed issue key, formal milestone or managed parent.
- Labels: `agent:ready`, `priority:p3`, `type:research`, `evidence:host`, `component:app-model`, `phase:m16-nativeaot`.
- Evidence prerequisite: qualified [M16-001 / #679](http://192.168.4.35:3000/admin/CLROS/issues/679), `done/step1198.md`. Related foundation: [#678](http://192.168.4.35:3000/admin/CLROS/issues/678).
- This is not a dependency of #684, the M16/M10 critical path or foundation closure. The stock Linux NativeAOT/Kestrel route remains primary; WASI HTTP is an optional different server contract, never a replacement for the mandatory Kestrel milestone by implication.

## Objective and scope

Determine whether a bounded .NET 11 WASI HTTP component could offer a smaller optional workload profile where the host owns TCP/HTTP acceptance and invokes an incoming request handler. Separately assess whether a narrow C# `IServer` adapter can invoke the ASP.NET Minimal API pipeline through `IHttpApplication<TContext>`. Distinguish these results from each other and from Kestrel.

Start with an explicit toolchain admission gate. Pin a .NET 11 NativeAOT-LLVM compiler/package set, WASM core/component tooling, WASI WIT version and host engine; list exact packages and native dependencies. A Linux NativeAOT RID is not WASM support. Stop at a reproducible compiler/runtime/component-model blocker if the required .NET 11 profile cannot be produced; do not silently substitute .NET7, Mono interpretation, a native-language handler or a kernel-authored HTTP response.

If the admission gate passes, publish the smallest .NET handler, then evaluate a custom `IServer` adapter with `/healthz` returning exact `OS_MINIMAL_API_OK`. Record exactly which ASP.NET HTTP features are implemented or rejected. Request/context creation, asynchronous processing, response completion, cancellation and context disposal must have explicit lifetimes. Keep the network accept loop in the host and measure the actual module imports rather than importing broad WASIX/POSIX services by default.

## Source and file scope

- Read `docs/workload-profiles.md`, `docs/kestrel.md`, `docs/app-model.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/license-audit.md`, `done/step1198.md` and applicable agent guides.
- Proposed experimental files: `apps/WasiHttpStudy/` and compiled host tooling in `tools/OS.WasiHttpStudy/`. Keep artifacts ignored, first-party source C#14/.NET11 and the default solution/workload profile unchanged. No EFI/kernel changes, native source imports, reference build inputs or general engine port in this issue.
- NativeAOT-LLVM research pin: [runtimelab 527a565752062b20bb9693eea6c884b34ecce7bf compilation instructions](https://github.com/dotnet/runtimelab/blob/527a565752062b20bb9693eea6c884b34ecce7bf/docs/using-nativeaot/compiling.md). This is an experimental branch, not the stock SDK NativeAOT target; resolve compatible package/tool versions before any build.
- Start with the existing [componentize-dotnet toolchain at f6bfc5a9a5a25728aeec959be60c8f737278a183](https://github.com/bytecodealliance/componentize-dotnet/tree/f6bfc5a9a5a25728aeec959be60c8f737278a183); its `Directory.Packages.props` pins experimental LLVM `10.0.0-rc.1.26306.1`, not the Linux baseline runtime 10.0.12. Resolve the package-to-source relationship explicitly. The [Spin ASP.NET example at 1e353c974c63e851b02d8d5d06947a0b769456fa](https://github.com/dicej/spin-dotnet-sdk/blob/1e353c974c63e851b02d8d5d06947a0b769456fa/samples/http-aspnetcore/App.cs) registers a custom IServer and its project targets net9.0; use it as an adaptation reference, not .NET 11 or Kestrel evidence.
- WASI HTTP research pin: [v0.2.3 / 3c1734c55239ccb700a1f61443047ab4cfa5deb5 handler.wit](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wasi-http/blob/3c1734c55239ccb700a1f61443047ab4cfa5deb5/wit/handler.wit). Use its request/response resource lifetimes and exported incoming-handler contract; document any adapter needed from a Preview 1 core module. Do not assume a Preview 1 command is a Preview 2 HTTP component.
- Engine candidate: [Wasmtime v44.0.0 / af382d7d946b3de82db4bb1f6065b565f97446ae](https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/tree/af382d7d946b3de82db4bb1f6065b565f97446ae), especially `docs/stability-platform-support.md` and `examples/min-platform/`. Host execution is the first experiment; a future minimal/offline-AOT custom-platform embedding still requires its own allocator, selected trap/TLS/platform hooks and C# capability imports. Bundled WASI is not a ready-made CLROS custom-target implementation.
- ASP.NET contract: [v10.0.12 IServer.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/v10.0.12/src/Hosting/Server.Abstractions/src/IServer.cs). Preserve license/provenance for every adapted source. WACS `cad6530f5d5765f5de79ca77ed166b99802372ea` is an optional managed-engine comparison only: its GC/EH/thread/BCL requirements must not be assumed available in the CLROS kernel.

## Acceptance

1. Preserve exact compiler/runtime/package/engine/WIT/source hashes, build commands, native dependencies and a complete module import/export/feature inventory: memory/limits, WASM EH/GC requirements, threads/shared memory/atomics, SIMD, and component adapters. Clearly distinguish the guest .NET GC from any engine/host GC. Record the CLR/BCL surface actually required by the handler and attempted ASP.NET profile.
2. Either demonstrate the actual .NET component returns HTTP200/exact body through a pinned host WASI incoming-handler invocation, or preserve a minimal reproducible admission blocker. Report separately whether a C# ASP.NET `IServer`/Minimal API pipeline ran; a Console output, hand-authored WAT module, standalone response handler or successful publish cannot satisfy that claim.
3. For each executing profile, test repeated requests, malformed/oversized input, response-body backpressure, cancellation/timeout and resource cleanup. Set explicit memory and execution/request budgets; include one exhausted-budget control and denied unavailable capability. Prove that runaway guest computation can be interrupted under the selected engine configuration and bound host imports independently.
   Run two independent host instances with separate capability/resource tables and verify one instance's trap/teardown does not corrupt the other's response; record that this is host engine isolation evidence only.
4. Produce a source-backed port-cost comparison against the qualified Linux payload: capability/import and guest runtime requirements, host-owned HTTP responsibilities, required ASP.NET feature coverage, compatibility limits, engine trusted code, offline-AOT versus interpretation, and unresolved freestanding hooks. A deliberately single-thread handler may avoid Linux thread/signal services; measure rather than assume it. Do not extrapolate host performance or sandbox checks into CLROS isolation/security superiority.
5. Deliver an adopt/defer/reject recommendation in a new reserved `done/stepNN.md` and existing `docs/kestrel.md`/`docs/app-model.md` research section. An evidenced negative feasibility result can close this research issue. Any future engine port, custom `IServer` production work or architecture change needs its own scoped ticket; no guest gate advances here.

## Commands and markers

Implement the proposed interface `dotnet run --project tools/OS.WasiHttpStudy -- qualify --output <fresh-directory>`; it does not exist yet. The C# driver records exact compiler/component/engine argument arrays, bounds subprocess output/time and cleans up only its owned children. Run `dotnet build tools/OS.WasiHttpStudy --nologo`, `dotnet run --project tools/OS.Tooling -- repo check`, `dotnet run --project tools/OS.Tooling -- contracts check`, and `git diff --check` after code changes.

Use `TEST_START wasi.http.study`, `TEST_PASS wasi.http.study` and `TEST_FAIL wasi.http.study <reason>` for executed checks. A blocked publish/import gate must emit failure and preserve its reason; closing the research report does not turn that run into a pass. Never emit Kestrel guest acceptance markers for this profile.

Boundary: optional host feasibility only. A custom `IServer` serving ASP.NET is not Kestrel; Wasmtime-hosted HTTP is not CLROS guest networking, multi-process isolation, cloud readiness or production qualification.


<!-- clros-canonical-review:2026-10-23 -->
## Current implementation requirements (2026-10-23)

- The title/toolchain are a deliberately historical .NET10 experiment, while repository first-party policy is now .NET11. Before implementation, select and document a compatible .NET11 experimental toolchain or record an admission blocker; do not silently rewrite old package pins or represent WASI/custom IServer as Kestrel/Linux compatibility.

This description is maintained in `supplementalIssues` in `.gitea/backlog/clros-issues.json`; preserve its existing issue identity and human addenda. Reference inspection supplies test ideas, not CLROS acceptance.
